- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong trend, forecast should revert toward 20-day moving average within 3–5 periods.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1) triggers early mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day average, not 30d.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, avoid overfitting to recent volatility — use 15d smoothing for horizon-specific forecasts.
